correctness.rationale: With dA=dxdy/pi and source norm log(e/(1-|z|^2))^alpha, angular integration makes the squared monomial norm v_k(alpha)=int_0^1 t^k log(e/(1-t))^alpha dt. The normalized Hilbert coefficient matrix has entries B_mk=1/((m+k+1)sqrt((m+1)v_k)); Tonelli gives its exact positive HS norm squared sum_{k>=0} S_k/v_k, S_k=sum_{m>=0}1/((m+1)(m+k+1)^2). For k>=1, partial fractions yield S_k=H_k/k^2-(zeta(2)-H_k^(2))/k, S_0=zeta(3). Independent high-precision summation confirmed this for k=1,2,5,20. The Laplace scaling s=k(1-t), with uniform logarithmic moments for alpha∈[2,3], gives v_k=(log k)^alpha/k(1+O(1/log k)); S_k=(log k+gamma-1+O(1/k))/k^2. Hence summands are 1/(k(log k)^(alpha-1))+O(1/(k(log k)^alpha)) uniformly near 2, with uniformly summable remainder; the integral test yields squared HS norm=1/(alpha-2)+O(1). For every fixed alpha≤2 the positive series diverges, while for alpha>2 it converges. Endpoint boundedness does not imply HS. The precise O(1) error and coefficient 1 are normalization-sensitive; no other Schatten exponent or singular-value distribution is proved.

However it does not provide the precise original Bergman monomial-moment normalization, the exact positive harmonic-number trace identity, or the uniform coefficient-one O(1) blow-up, which require additional summation and uniform moment control. The surviving claim is this exact quantitative supercritical norm law, not new compactness, boundedness, or an endpoint HS perturbation.
